editorial.headline: Public Higher Education Is Not an Open PMA Route
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers government-run higher education, from diploma to doctoral level, but is closed to foreign investment nationally and listed as closed for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
Government General Higher Education is the public provision of tertiary education: diploma, bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral programmes, alongside equivalent academic, professional and vocational education. Its stated purpose is broad intellectual development across science, technology, the arts and the humanities. The setting is equally specific: this is education delivered by government through universities, institutes and higher-education schools.

The activity is open across the recorded business scales—micro, small, medium and large—but scale should not be mistaken for an invitation to foreign ownership. Nationally, the PMA status is closed and the maximum foreign ownership is 0%. In practical terms, a foreign investor does not have a foreign-equity route into this activity under the national position recorded here. The relevant national references are Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021.

Bali does not soften that conclusion. The provincial status is also listed as closed, and the Bali record marks PMA registration as blocked. A foreigner therefore cannot register this activity in Bali today. The accompanying Bali note adds an important distinction: the activity is described as medium-high or high risk and is not blocked by the province-wide moratorium itself; the position should be verified for the specific address. That moratorium applies island-wide and permanently to all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA, but it is not the stated basis for this activity’s Bali outcome.

That distinction matters because it keeps the analysis disciplined. The national position is a closed PMA classification with no foreign ownership permitted. Bali’s recorded result is likewise closed for PMA, while its note points to risk classification and address-level verification rather than the provincial moratorium. For founders, the clearest reading is also the most useful: government-run higher education may span every listed enterprise scale, but it is not available as a foreign-owned registration pathway, nationally or in Bali.
